thesis.company_overview:
Tenet Healthcare Corporation (THC) is a Dallas-headquartered diversified healthcare services company operating across the U.S. acute-care and ambulatory-care delivery chain, with a Global Business Center in the Philippines supporting enterprise-wide administrative functions. The company monetizes patient volumes through its hospital and outpatient networks, earning revenue from third-party payors and patients; TTM revenue stands at $21.81B with a TTM operating margin of 19.5% and TTM EBITDA of $5.31B, the service-heavy, low-cost-of-goods profile typical of healthcare providers.

A segment revenue breakdown was not available for this issuer; see the latest annual report for business-line detail. Qualitatively the franchise spans acute-care hospitals and a large ambulatory-surgery platform, but we do not attribute revenue shares to these lines in the absence of sourceable segment data. Geographic revenue breakdown was likewise not available from the supplied filings; reporting is predominantly U.S.-centric, with the only disclosed non-U.S. footprint being the administrative Global Business Center, and we therefore cite no geographic revenue split.

The durable moat rests on scale, local market density and payor-contracting leverage rather than differentiated IP: high fixed-cost hospital assets create barriers to entry, and the ambulatory-surgery footprint adds a lower-capital, higher-margin growth vector. That said, the moat is reimbursement-exposed — pricing power is set largely by government programs and commercial payor negotiations, not by the company. Credit quality reinforces the profile, with a Merton distance to default of 3.52 and a 0.02% one-year default probability.
thesis.competitor_analysis: No peer set was produced for this run — the peer-screen / peer-financials data fetch returned no usable comps for this ticker, so all relative-multiple commentary here is benchmarked against Tenet's own trading history rather than direct competitors, and we make no peer-relative over/undervaluation claim. On that internal yardstick the current ~7.0x operating EV/EBITDA sits above the stock's own 5-year median of 6.2x, a positioning the technical chapter explicitly classifies as expensive. The 9.76x TTM parent-earnings multiple and 19.5% TTM operating margin describe a scale hospital operator whose economics are reimbursement-driven and volume-sensitive rather than differentiated by IP. Absent a corroborated peer multiple set, we treat the competitive comparison as qualitative and lean on the DCF / EV-EBITDA dispersion — not peer-relative valuation — for the HOLD.

thesis.narrative:
Tenet Healthcare at $271.60 is a genuinely two-sided valuation case. Our DCF — WACC 7.45%, a 10-year revenue fade from 3.6% in forecast year 1 to 3.0% in year 10 (3.3% average) into a 3.0% perpetuity — discounts to an implied $541.80 per share (range $433.44–$650.16), while the EV/EBITDA cross-check, reverting the current ~7.0x multiple toward the stock's own 5-year median of 6.2x, lands at $212.91 (range $120.36–$305.46). With the surviving method mids spanning a 2.5x spread and the published band of $212.91–$541.80 straddling spot, no single point is publishable; we initiate at HOLD with the point target withheld.

The operating base is solid, if not accelerating. TTM revenue of $21.81B supports TTM EBITDA of $5.31B and a 19.5% TTM operating margin, and credit risk is de minimis — a Merton distance to default of 3.52 and a 0.02% one-year default probability on 37.7% market leverage. The equity trades at 9.76x TTM parent net income and 6.96x operating EBITDA, a multiple the technical band flags at ~7.0x versus its own 6.2x median, i.e. at the expensive end of its own history.

Price action already reflects much of the good news: +42.9% over the trailing year, a 91% 52-week range position and just -4.0% off the 52-week high. The market's own reverse-DCF, holding the model's 7.45% WACC, implies revenue shrinking ~-2.6%/yr flat over 10 years — a materially more bearish construct than the model's own 3.3%/yr average fade, which is precisely why the DCF sits above the tape while the multiple-based method sits below it. That -2.6% flat versus 3.3% fade gap is the crux of the HOLD.
thesis.news_summary: News flow over the trailing 30-day window (50 items, 2026-09-08 through 2026-10-10) is net bullish, with an aggregate catalyst sentiment score of +1.75 and no negative-catalyst items logged. The dominant positive is Tenet's upgrade of full-year 2026 revenue guidance following its latest operating results (2026-10-06, impact score 5), a genuinely thesis-moving event rather than a routine headline. A 2026-09-22 SEC 8-K disclosing a material agreement and a material financial obligation rounds out the primary-source flow, though it is classified neutral at impact 3. The guidance raise is consistent with the operating base — TTM revenue $21.81B and TTM EBITDA $5.31B — but with the shares up +42.9% over the trailing year and sitting at 91% of their 52-week range, much of that news is already reflected in the $271.60 price. Net, the news backdrop is supportive but not sufficient to break the valuation stalemate that drives the HOLD.

Method dispersion is itself the risk: a 2.5x spread between the DCF ($541.80 mid) and EV/EBITDA ($212.91 mid) means fair value is highly assumption-sensitive, with the 0.85-weighted DCF dominated by its terminal value rather than near-term cash flow.

thesis.tagline: THC · Fairly valued; HOLD on a 2.5x method spread
thesis.valuation_overview:
Two methods survive, and they frame rather than resolve the call. The DCF — WACC 7.45%, revenue fading from 3.6% in forecast year 1 to 3.0% in year 10 (3.3% average) and a 3.0% perpetuity — implies $541.80, well above the $271.60 price, because the projection keeps Tenet's cash flows growing through the explicit window, whereas the market's own reverse-DCF, holding that same 7.45% WACC, implies a flat ~-2.6%/yr revenue path over 10 years. The EV/EBITDA method implies $212.91, below spot, because reverting the current ~7.0x multiple toward the stock's own 5-year median of 6.2x compresses the multiple even on unchanged TTM EBITDA of $5.31B.

The two mids differ by 2.5x — a spread that exceeds the 2x corroboration limit — so no single point merits headline status; the published band is the span of the method mids, $212.91–$541.80, which straddles the current price. Weighting does not rescue the gap: the DCF carries 0.85 weight and the multiple method 0.72, but confidence is only medium and the DCF's value is dominated by its terminal component. The honest conclusion is that the stock is fairly valued within a wide range, which is why the HOLD is directional rather than point-anchored.
